supporting_observations.claim: The supplied records show recurring CONNECT attempts to update.chartmate-imaging.net:443 at 13:38:00, 13:43:20, 13:47:44, 13:52:37, 13:58:16, 14:03:02 and 14:08:00 UTC, consistent with the alerted roughly five-minute pattern.

Endpoint network events and matching Zeek source ports attribute these proxy connections to PID 3416, C:\Users\ben.carter\AppData\Local\ChartMate\cmupdate.exe, running as ben.carter. For example, source port 51599 links the 13:38 connection, and source port 50420 links the 14:08 connection.

The observed executable path and destination differ from the supplied approved ChartMate configuration: the process runs from the user's AppData directory rather than C:\Program Files\ChartMate\cmupdate.exe, and contacts a .net domain rather than the approved update.chartmate-imaging.com. The matching product name and cadence therefore do not establish approved updater activity.

PID 3416 was launched by explorer.exe at 13:37:57 with --background under ben.carter at medium integrity. A subsequent file-creation event attributes creation or overwrite of its own executable path to that PID at 13:38:01; this event alone does not establish malicious self-modification.

Five CONNECT requests received status 200 and logged identical tunnel byte counts of 5,397 client-to-server and 31,383 server-to-client bytes. The 13:43 request instead received proxy authentication-required status 407, and the 13:52 request received gateway-error status 502; those two attempts are not evidence of successful outbound HTTPS tunnels.

The path/domain discrepancies warrant investigation of the alerted activity, but periodicity, repeated byte counts and a ChartMate-like executable name do not distinguish an unauthorized or malicious impersonator from an undocumented legitimate installation.

known_telemetry_limitations: The successful proxy records expose CONNECT targets and tunnel metadata, not decrypted requests, responses or transferred content (T015-00110, T015-00209, T015-00264, T015-00269, T015-00281).
The process-creation and file-creation records do not provide executable hashes, signature validation, vendor provenance or file contents (T015-00108, T015-00109, T015-00114).

The supplied recurring connection records cover 13:38 through 14:08, not the entire interval described in the alert; they do not independently demonstrate this pattern beginning at 13:30 (T015-00110, T015-00152, T015-00209, T015-00234, T015-00264, T015-00269, T015-00281).
claims_not_established: Whether the AppData executable is authentic ChartMate software, an undocumented deployment or an impersonating binary (T015-00108, T015-00114).
Whether update.chartmate-imaging.net is vendor-controlled or authorized; the observed destination differs from the supplied approved .com endpoint (T015-00110, T015-00281).
Whether the successful tunnels carried update checks, command-and-control traffic, sensitive data or other content (T015-00110, T015-00209, T015-00264, T015-00269, T015-00281).
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire the AppData cmupdate.exe, calculate its hash, validate its digital signature and compare it with a trusted vendor package; inspect the file event at 13:38:01 (T015-00108, T015-00114).
Verify with the software owner and vendor whether the AppData installation path and update.chartmate-imaging.net endpoint are legitimate and approved (T015-00108, T015-00110).

Obtain available TLS certificate, upstream destination and decrypted proxy or endpoint application telemetry for the successful tunnels to determine their purpose and content (T015-00110, T015-00209, T015-00264, T015-00269, T015-00281).

Retrieve installer/download provenance and earlier endpoint/proxy records to explain the executable's origin and reconcile the alert's 13:30 start with the first supplied recurring connection at 13:38 (T015-00108, T015-00110).
unrelated_findings: For a separate ticket, review the anonymous NTLM network logon to FILE-HD-01 from WS-BCARTER-01 at 13:54:48. The supplied records show an SMB connection and ANONYMOUS LOGON but do not link it to PID 3416 or establish malicious access; it does not decide this alert (T015-00253, T015-00254, T015-00257).
